musclesWorked: Piriformis and deep hip rotators (front leg, external rotation)

description.en: A seated hip mobility drill with both legs on the floor at 90-degree angles: the front leg in external rotation and the back leg in internal rotation.

en: Sit on the floor. Bend your right knee to 90 degrees in front of you with the outside of your right leg on the floor.
Bend your left knee to 90 degrees behind you with the inside of your left leg on the floor.
Sit up tall and square your torso forward over your right shin.
For a deeper stretch, lean forward over your right shin, keeping your back flat.
Hold for 30 to 60 seconds, then switch sides.
Stretches both hip internal and external rotation at once
Improves squat depth and hip-hinge flexibility
No equipment needed

description.en: The barbell bench press is the most popular upper-body pressing exercise in strength training. It primarily develops the pectoralis major while heavily recruiting the front deltoids and triceps.

en: Lie back on a flat bench with your eyes directly under the bar. Plant both feet firmly on the floor.
Pull your shoulder blades down and back, pinning them to the bench.
Grip the bar with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width and stack your wrists over your elbows.
Unrack the bar with straight arms, take a deep breath and brace your core.
Lower the bar under control to the lower portion of your chest, elbows at roughly 45 to 75 degrees from your torso.
Press the bar back up and slightly toward your face, finishing with your arms straight over your shoulders.
Builds size and strength in the chest, front deltoids, and triceps
One of the most reliable measures of upper-body pressing strength
Allows progressive overload across a long career of training

description.en: The heel glute bridge is a glute bridge variation performed with the toes lifted off the floor and weight pushed through the heels only. The toes-up position increases hamstring activation while still loading the glutes heavily.

en: Lie flat on your back with knees bent at 90 degrees and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Lift your toes off the floor. Keep only your heels in contact with the ground.
Brace your core. Press your lower back into the floor.
Drive through your heels and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips off the floor.
Continue lifting until your body forms a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Squeeze your glutes and hamstrings hard at the top for one to two seconds.
Lower under control back to the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of reps. Aim for 12 to 20 reps per set.
